previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson, a male with a history of kidney transplant, atrial fibrillation, heart failure with preserved ejection fraction, and coronary artery disease, was admitted for worsening dyspnea, cough, and 6-pound weight gain following a recent upper respiratory infection. Evaluation revealed acute on chronic diastolic heart failure, a moderate pericardial effusion with early signs of tamponade physiology, and elevated inflammatory markers suggestive of viral pericarditis. Diuresis was initially held to maintain cardiac preload, and he was started on aspirin and colchicine for pericarditis. Once the effusion stabilized, diuresis was resumed with IV Lasix and metolazone, achieving a dry weight of 85 kg. Empiric antibiotics were given for possible pneumonia, though cultures remained negative. His torsemide dose was increased to 80 mg twice daily, hydralazine was added for hypertension, and tacrolimus was reduced per nephrology. He improved clinically, was discharged home with close follow-up, and advised to monitor weight and symptoms.
problems: Acute on chronic diastolic (congestive) heart failure
Hypertensive heart and chronic kidney disease with heart failure
